art.subject: Isabelline Shrike (Lanius isabellinus), adult male in autumn: crown and upperparts pale sandy grey-buff; a black mask from the lores through the eye to the ear-coverts, with a faint pale supercilium above it; wings brownish-black with pale fringes and a small white patch at the base of the primaries; rump and tail rufous-orange, contrasting with the pale back; underparts creamy white with a pinkish-buff wash on the breast and flanks. Bill dark and hooked; dark eye; legs dark grey.
art.pose: perched upright on top of a low bush, side view
art.scene: Dry scrubby field edge on the Korean coast in October, autumn migration, warm low light; no people, buildings or text
art.build: Small, slim shrike, about the size of Brown Shrike, with a longish, slightly graduated tail; perches upright on bush tops. Bill short, strong and hooked. Legs short, dark. Females are duller, with a browner mask, a smaller or no white wing patch and faint dark crescents on the breast sides; first-winter birds resemble females.
avoid: Do not paint warm rufous-brown upperparts or a bold white supercilium; those mark Brown Shrike (Lanius cristatus).
Do not paint a rufous crown; that marks Red-tailed Shrike (Lanius phoenicuroides).
Do not paint a grey crown with a chestnut back (Red-backed Shrike).
Do not make the tail the same colour as the back; the rufous tail contrasts with the pale sandy body.
